A 33-year-old female patient with no significant medical history presented to the Dermatology Department with a nodule that had enlarged over the past four years, arising within a congenital alopecic plaque.
A skin biopsy was obtained from both the verrucous plaque and the nodular lesion.
The plaque biopsy demonstrated epidermal papillomatosis with acanthosis associated with an increase in sebaceous glands and abortive hair follicles, consistent with nevus sebaceous (Figure 2).
Complete surgical excision of the lesions was performed (Figure 5A-5C).
At the three-month follow-up, there was no evidence of recurrence.

A 33-year-old female patient with no significant medical history presented to the Dermatology Department with a nodule that had enlarged over the past four years, arising within a congenital alopecic plaque.
Physical examination revealed a 6 x 2.5 x 0.2 cm, pink to brown, verrucous plaque with sharp borders.
Also, a 1.2 x 1 x 1 cm, pink, multilobulated, pedunculated nodule with a firm consistency was found at the lower end of the plaque (Figures 1A, 1B).
A skin biopsy was obtained from both the verrucous plaque and the nodular lesion.

summary.text: A 33-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented to dermatology with a nodule that had enlarged over four years within a congenital, long-standing alopecic plaque on the scalp. Examination showed a 6 x 2.5 x 0.2 cm pink to brown verrucous plaque with sharp borders, placed by the figure caption on the right parietal scalp, and a 1.2 x 1 x 1 cm pink, multilobulated, pedunculated, firm nodule at its lower end.

Skin biopsy was taken from the plaque and the nodule. The plaque showed epidermal papillomatosis with acanthosis, increased sebaceous glands and abortive hair follicles, and a basaloid follicular proliferation with peripheral palisading; the nodule showed small cuboidal basaloid cells with ductal differentiation. These findings were consistent with nevus sebaceous, trichoblastoma and eccrine poroma, diagnosed as arising within a nevus sebaceous.
Complete surgical excision of the lesions was performed, with the plaque and nodule removed in a single specimen with clear margins. At the three-month follow-up there was no evidence of recurrence.
